   STAFF REPORT:                 Review and Approve Annual Report


   SUBJECT:                      Annual Report to Governor



INTRODUCTION

Per California Public Resource Code 535, “the commission shall report annually to
the Governor, through the director, on existing and operating recreational facilities,
programs and activities of the state park system, and on the needs of the state and
the local subdivisions thereof for recreational facilities, programs, and activities, and
shall make recommendations for programs and activities to meet future needs of the
state for parks and recreation.


DESCRIPTION

The Annual Report to the Governor before the State Park and Recreation Commission is
for the period of January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2025. The Annual Report
summarizes all the Commission’s actions during that period along with the Commission’s
priorities.

NEXT STEPS

Once approved, the final version will be sent to the Governor’s Office.

RECOMMENDATION

Recommend approval of the Annual Report.

COMMISSION ACTION(S)

Upon review, the Commission may suggest updates, approve, or send back to
subcommittee for additional work.

   STAFF REPORT:                 Budget Report


   SUBJECT:                      2026-27 Governor’s Budget



OBJECTIVE
Update on Department of Parks and Recreation (State Parks) 2026 Proposed Budget.
INTRODUCTION

The Governor released his proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year on January 9th,
2026.

DESCRIPTION

Overview

The 2026-27 Governor’s Budget includes $1.008 billion to support the Department of Parks
and Recreation. Of this amount, $860.9 million is available for state operations, $135.6
million is available for local assistance, and $11.03 million is available for Capital Outlay
projects. The proposed budget includes $223.8 million General Fund (GF) and $296.3
million State Parks and Recreation Fund (SPRF) to support operations and local
assistance.

Overall, the 2026 proposed budget reflects a $451 million decrease from the 2025 enacted
budget. The majority of this reduction is attributable to one-time Proposition 4 funds that
were appropriated in the prior year for local assistance grants and various projects. The
remaining decrease is associated with statewide budget adjustments and the expiration of
various one-time Budget Change Proposals (BCPs).

Climate Bond Update

The proposed budget includes Proposition 4 funding for the 2026-27 fiscal year, which
allocates funds to the following five programs:

   •   Deferred Maintenance: $400,000

       $33,400,000

Budget Change Proposals

State Operations & Local Assistance

California Indian Heritage Center — Access and Community

Funding Request: $842,000 one-time funding, 3.0 Permanent positions (2.0 Park and
Recreation Specialist, 1.0 Staff Services Manager I), and $805,000 ongoing from the
General Fund.

Request Summary:
  • Supports staff to plan and run public programs, tribal events, and community
     partnerships at the CIHC.
  • Helps deliver culturally meaningful education and interpretation shaped by Native
     communities.
  • Grows programs over time to build steady visitation and increase public awareness.
  • Ensures staff are in place to handle logistics, contracts, and ongoing coordination
     with Tribal partners as the CIHC opens.

California State Parks Library Pass Program

Funding Request: $6.75 million ongoing transfer from General Fund to State Parks
Recreation Fund.

Request Summary:
  • Converts from one-time funding to ongoing transfer.
  • Partners with the State Library and local libraries to provide free state park day-use
     passes, especially for communities with limited access to parks.
  • Ensures Tribal and rural communities can continue accessing passes through
     participating libraries.

Chaptered Legislation Proposals — Off-Highway Electric Motorcycles (SB 586)

     statewide electrification and sustainable recreation goals.

   STAFF REPORT:                 Northern Buttes District Update


   SUBJECT:                      Northern Buttes District Update



OBJECTIVE
To provide the State Park and Recreation Commission with a high-level administrative and
operational overview of the Northern Buttes District (NBD or District), featuring unit
statistics, significant cultural and natural resources, and District highlights.

INTRODUCTION

The Northern Buttes District (NBD) is a sprawling and diverse landscape encompassing
nine northern California counties. Our jurisdiction stretches across the northern
Sacramento River valley, the rugged northern Sierra foothills, the volcanic Cascade
mountains, and the ancient basin of Clear Lake, encompassing more than 27,000 square
miles. The total State parkland within that area is approximately 45,700 acres.

From the roaring 129-foot cascades of McArthur-Burney Falls—famously dubbed the
"eighth wonder of the world"—to the iconic silhouettes of the Sutter Buttes, often called the
"smallest mountain range in the world," our district offers a tapestry of California’s most
remarkable landmarks. We manage a total of 15 units, including six State Parks (SP), five
State Historic Parks (SHP), three State Recreation Areas (SRA), and one State Vehicular
Recreation Area (SVRA).

The recreation opportunities within the district are as varied as the terrain itself. Visitors can
enjoy world-class trout fishing in the upper Sacramento River, explore 90 miles of multi-use
trails at Lake Oroville, boat into the volcanic wilderness of Ahjumawi, or experience
centuries of cultural history at the oldest continuously used Chinese temple in California.
Whether it is backcountry camping among 6,000-foot granite spires or staying the night on
a floating campsite, NBD provides a premier destination for every type of outdoor

    Cascade Sector: Volcanic Spires and Sacred Springs

•   Castle Crags State Park: Named for the dramatic 6,000-foot glacier-polished crags, this
    3,904-acre park offers 28 miles of trails, 76 developed campsites and historic CCC-built
    infrastructure. Swimming and fishing in the upper Sacramento River are popular activities.
    The park is located just south of the community of Dunsmuir and is supported by the
    McArthur-Burney Falls Interpretive Association through their Friends of Castle Crags group.

•   McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial SP: Centered on the spectacular 129-foot Burney Falls,
    which is fed by an underground spring and holds deep sacred significance for the Pit River
    Tribe. The 1,013-acre park offers 116 campsites, a group campground, primitive sites, and
    cabins, along with five miles of hiking trails and a section of the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT).
    Fun fact: Section O of the PCT is an 80-mile link between McArthur-Burney Falls MSP and
    Castle Crags SP. The park is located near the gateway community of Burney and is
    supported by the McArthur-Burney Falls Interpretive Association. In 2024, the park signed a
    MOU with the Pit River Tribe to promote shared stewardship of their ancestral lands. The
    park also has a long-standing concession that operates the camp store, cabins, and
    marina.

•   Ahjumawi Lava Springs SP: This 6,400-acre park is accessible only by boat and protects
    one of the nation's largest freshwater spring systems. The park is named for the Ahjumawi
    people, an indigenous band of the Pit River Tribe who have lived there for thousands of
    years and still maintain cultural ties to the land. Camping is available at 3 designated
    environmental campgrounds with pit toilets with 3 campsites at each location. The park is
    nearest the communities of Fall River Mills and McArthur. The park was also included in the
    2024 MOU with Pit River Tribe.

•   Shasta SHP: Preserves the brick ruins of the "Queen City" of the northern mining district,
    featuring the restored 1861 Courthouse Museum and California artwork. The centerpiece of
    the park is the restored 1861 Courthouse Museum, which houses a visitor center, historical
    exhibits, and a large collection of California artwork, tours and interpretive programs. The
    park is located just east of Redding and is supported by the Town of Shasta Interpretive

   SUBJECT:                      Status of various Trail Plans



OBJECTIVE
To update the State Park and Recreation Commission on the various Trail Plans as well as
other projects that are happening within the State Park System and the State.
INTRODUCTION

This report describes the purpose and goals of current Trail Plans and other projects that
are underway within the Statewide Trails Office.

DESCRIPTION

Trione-Annadel State Park Road and Trail Management Plan

This Road and Trail Management Plan (RTMP) is a comprehensive planning document that
examines Trione-Annadel State Park’s existing road and trail system to provide direction for
long-term planning, design, construction, maintenance, and management. It considers
current and potential public use, park operations, and the protection and enhancement of
cultural and natural resources to ensure recreational trail opportunities are available to their
fullest potential while protecting vital resources. The Draft Plan was released on January
29, 2026, with the second public meeting held on February 4, 2026. Public comments were
due by February 27, 2026. Staff is reviewing the public comments received and working
towards the Environmental Document. The RTMP should be completed by early 2027.
Please visit the Trione-Annadel RTMP website for more information and send any other
project-related questions or concerns to trails@parks.ca.gov.

Big Basin Regional Road and Trail Management Plan

The Santa Cruz District is in the beginning stages of developing their Regional Road and

California Trails & Greenways Training

California Trails & Greenways provides high-quality education and networking opportunities
for urban, rural, and backcountry trail professionals. Join leading trail experts for training
and discussions on the latest advances in trail design, construction, maintenance,
interpretation, volunteerism, and management. Explore new, collaborative opportunities
and engage in productive, meaningful, and inspiring dialogue.

All activities are designed to increase the knowledge of trail, recreation, and wild land
management to improve trail systems and programs throughout California.

This training will be provided April 14 – 17, 2026 at the Marriott San Ramon.

Recreational Trails Plan Update

The Statewide Trails Office has partnered with the California Natural Resources Agency to
launch a statewide effort to improve access to recreational trails, like hiking, biking, and
horseback riding routes, especially for communities that have historically had less access
to them. This effort is part of a larger plan to make the outdoors more inclusive and
accessible, support climate resilience, honor tribal priorities, and help meet California’s
30x30 goal of protecting 30% of land and coastal water by 2030.

The are currently two surveys available. One survey is for community members to be able
to provide feedback regarding need and access and the other survey is for trail
professionals to be able to share their knowledge and experience within their local area.

Information gained from this community outreach will help inform the Recreation Trails
Plan. The Plan will include a new section based on regions of the state, with ideas and
considerations for providing local access to communities.

For information only

      SUBJECT:                      New Authorities for Land Acquisition



OBJECTIVE
To share information about new authorities granted to Department of Parks and Recreation
(DPR) to acquire new lands.

INTRODUCTION

DPR acquires land to create and expand the State Park units. Until January 1, 2026, DPR
has not held authority to acquire land without the review and approval of the State Public
Works Board, Department of General Services and Department of Finance. As of January
1, 2026, DPR has been granted two new authorities to acquire land.
DESCRIPTION

A PowerPoint presentation describing the three pathways by which DPR can acquire land,
including the two new authorities.
NEXT STEPS

DPR’s Acquisition and Real Property Services Division are acquiring land to expand
existing park units using the new authorities. Public announcements will be made as
acquisitions are completed. The first biennial report will be submitted by December 31,
2027, to the California Legislature regarding properties acquired with the new authorities.

RECOMMENDATION

The agenda item is informational; no recommendation offered.

COMMISSION ACTION(S)

n/a

   SUBJECT:                      State Park and Recreation Commission Approval of Memorial

INTRODUCTION

The State Park and Recreation Commission (SPRC or Commission) has specific authority
and responsibility to approve resolutions accepting and naming memorial redwood groves
and memorial trails in units of the State Park System. (Commission Policy 11.2)

DESCRIPTION

Sempervirens Fund is requesting approval from SPRC for the following Memorial Grove:

            •   01-2026 Peter Rieman’s Redwood Grove

Save the Redwoods League is requesting approval from SPRC for the following Memorial
Groves:

            •   02-2026 Calflin Generations
            •   03-2026 Shelley and Nick Robinson

RESULT OF NO ACTION BY COMMISSION

If there is no action by the Commission, these requests to recognize the memorial groves
will be delayed until the next Commission meeting.

RECOMMENDATION

Recommend the Commission approve the Memorial Grove Resolution.

COMMISSION ACTION(S)

Commission to approve via the consent calendar or remove from the consent calendar for
further discussion. Commission may approve, deny, or reschedule the hearing at a future
Commission Meeting.
